Wakefield left in 1998, and after the band struggled to find a replacement, a mutual contact recommended Bennington, who joined in 1999. plain: Japan has many specific terms for its traditional art forms. Ikebana refers to the art of flower arranging, emphasizing balance and natural form. Origami is paper folding, ranging from simple cranes to complex geometric designs. Shodo is the practice of calligraphy, using brush and ink to write characters expressively. Ukiyo-e describes woodblock prints depicting scenes of everyday life, landscapes, and kabuki actors, popular in the Edo period. Sumi-e is monochrome ink wash painting, often of nature scenes, valued for its minimalism. Bonsai, cultivating miniature trees, is considered both horticulture and art. Chanoyu, or the tea ceremony, blends ritual, aesthetics, and hospitality. Noh and Kabuki are traditional theater forms combining music, dance, and elaborate costumes. Each of these reflects broader Japanese aesthetic values like simplicity, seasonality, and mindful attention to detail.

He measured two scoops of ground coffee into the French press, not more, not less. When the kettle whistled, he poured the water in slowly, waited four minutes, then pressed the plunger down. He poured the coffee into his mug, added a splash of milk, and carried it to the table. He sat down, looked out the window at the gray morning, and took a sip. plain: In the United States, streets are generally classified by their function and traffic level. Local streets (or residential streets) serve individual homes and have low speeds and light traffic. Collector streets gather traffic from local streets and funnel it toward larger roads, often seen near schools or shopping areas. Arterial roads are wider, higher-capacity routes designed to move traffic across a city, usually with higher speed limits and multiple lanes. Highways and freeways are the largest category, built for long-distance, high-speed travel with limited access points and no cross traffic. There are also specialized types like cul-de-sacs (dead-end streets with a circular turnaround), alleys (narrow service ways behind buildings), and boulevards (wide, often landscaped streets with medians). Numbered grid streets are common in cities like Manhattan or Salt Lake City, following a systematic layout.

plain: Power in a Muay Thai roundhouse kick comes mostly from hip rotation, not just leg strength. As you kick, pivot fully on the standing foot so your hip can rotate through the target, turning your whole body sideways rather than just swinging your leg. Drive the power up from the ground through your legs and core, using the twist of your torso to add momentum. Keep your shin, not your foot, as the striking surface for a harder, less injury-prone impact. Swing your arms in opposition to help generate rotational speed, and snap through the target rather than aiming to stop at it, since follow-through adds significant force. Strong hip flexors, glutes, and core muscles built through squats, hip rotations, and heavy bag drills all contribute to a consistently powerful kick over time.

plain: Some of the best vegan protein sources include lentils and beans (about 15-18 grams of protein per cooked cup), tofu and tempeh (roughly 10-20 grams per half-cup, with tempeh being denser and higher in protein), and edamame (about 17 grams per cup). Seitan, made from wheat gluten, is especially protein-dense at around 25 grams per 100 grams. Quinoa offers a complete amino acid profile with about 8 grams per cooked cup, and it works well as a base for meals. Nuts, seeds, and nut butters, particularly peanuts, almonds, and hemp seeds, add protein along with healthy fats. Plant-based protein powders (pea, soy, or rice-based) can help fill gaps, especially for athletes. Combining a variety of these sources across the day generally covers all essential amino acids without needing to plan every meal precisely.

But banning it entirely is hard to enforce and ignores real benefits: it can help students brainstorm, get instant feedback on drafts, practice language skills, or explain concepts in a different way when a teacher isn't available. A more workable approach is for schools to set clear rules about when AI use is appropriate versus when it counts as academic dishonesty, redesign some assignments so they're harder to complete with AI alone (like in-class writing or oral defenses), and actively teach students how to use these tools responsibly, since they'll likely encounter them throughout their careers regardless of school policy.

plain: The four major championships in men's professional golf, often called 'the majors,' are the Masters Tournament, held every April at Augusta National Golf Club in Georgia; the PGA Championship, typically played in May; the U.S. Open, held in June and organized by the USGA, known for its brutally difficult course setups; and The Open Championship (often called the British Open), held in July, the oldest of the four, dating back to 1860, and played on links-style courses in the UK. Winning all four in a calendar year would complete the modern 'Grand Slam,' something no golfer has achieved, though Tiger Woods held all four titles simultaneously across two seasons in 2000-2001, sometimes called the 'Tiger Slam.' These four events carry the most prestige and historical weight in the sport, separate from tournaments organized directly by the PGA Tour.

plain: To make meetings more efficient, start with a clear agenda sent out in advance so attendees know what will be discussed and can prepare. Only invite people who actually need to be there, since large groups slow down decision-making. Set a firm start and end time, and actually stick to it, since a scheduled hour tends to expand to fill whatever time is available. Assign someone to keep the discussion on track and gently redirect tangents to a separate follow-up conversation. End with clear action items, owners, and deadlines, rather than letting the meeting end vaguely. Consider whether the meeting needs to happen at all, since updates that don't require real-time discussion can often be handled through a written message instead. Finally, default to shorter meetings, like 25 or 45 minutes instead of 30 or 60, to build in natural breathing room between calls.

plain: The most convenient way to get from London to Paris is the Eurostar high-speed train, which runs directly between St Pancras International in London and Gare du Nord in central Paris in about 2 hours and 15 minutes. It's generally faster door-to-door than flying once you account for airport check-in, security, and the transfer into central Paris from Charles de Gaulle. Flying is an option if you find a cheap fare, taking about 1 hour and 15 minutes in the air, but total travel time often ends up similar to or longer than the train. Driving and taking a ferry across the Channel is possible too, useful if you want a car in France, but it takes considerably longer, around 6-7 hours depending on traffic and crossing times. For most travelers without a car, booking Eurostar tickets in advance for a better price is the simplest and most comfortable choice.

plain: Enzo Ferrari worked for Alfa Romeo for many years, first as a driver and then running Alfa's racing division, Scuderia Ferrari, which managed the company's motorsport program starting in 1929. Tensions grew through the 1930s as Alfa Romeo brought its racing operations back in-house and reduced Ferrari's autonomy, particularly after appointing a new managing director whose management style clashed with Ferrari's. Ferrari also felt sidelined as younger engineers were promoted into roles he felt should have gone to people loyal to him. He formally left Alfa Romeo in 1939, reportedly under an agreement that barred him from using his own name on cars or racing for four years. He used that time to found Auto Avio Costruzioni, which built its first car in 1940, and once the restriction period ended, he launched Ferrari as we know it, producing his first car under that name in 1947.

plain: Proper concrete prep is the most important factor in whether epoxy coating lasts. Start by cleaning the surface thoroughly, removing dust, oil, grease, and any old paint or sealer, since epoxy won't bond to anything sitting on top of the concrete. Next, mechanically profile the surface, usually with a diamond grinder or shot blaster, to open up the concrete's pores and create a rough texture (roughly the texture of 60-grit sandpaper) that gives the epoxy something to grip. Acid etching is a cheaper alternative to grinding but generally gives a weaker, less consistent profile. After grinding, vacuum thoroughly and check the moisture level with a moisture meter or plastic sheet test, since trapped moisture can cause the epoxy to bubble or delaminate later. Repair any cracks or holes with an appropriate filler and let it cure fully. Finally, make sure the concrete is fully cured, ideally at least 28 days old if it's new, before applying epoxy.

plain: Easter festivities vary by culture but share some common themes. In many Western countries, families dye and decorate eggs, symbolizing new life and rebirth, and children take part in egg hunts where hidden eggs (real or chocolate) are searched for around the house or yard. The Easter Bunny is a popular figure for kids, delivering baskets filled with candy and small gifts. Many people attend church services, especially sunrise services, to mark the religious significance of Christ's resurrection, and families often gather for a large meal, commonly featuring ham or lamb. In some countries, like parts of Europe, there are traditions like Easter bonfires, water fights (as in Poland's Smigus-Dyngus), or elaborate processions during Holy Week, particularly in Spain and Latin America. Easter parades, featuring decorated bonnets and floats, are also a tradition in some U.S. cities like New York.

plain: It depends heavily on who your users are and what the product does. If this is an internal tool, API, or something aimed at technical users who are comfortable with a CLI or raw endpoints, releasing without a UI and adding one later is reasonable and lets you validate the core functionality faster. But calling it 'GA' (generally available) without a UI is riskier if your actual target audience is non-technical, since GA implies the product is ready for broad, unsupported use, and a missing UI often means significant support burden and poor adoption. A middle path is to ship a minimal, even ugly, UI that covers the core workflow, then call that GA, while treating a polished UI as a fast-follow improvement rather than blocking GA on it entirely. I'd push back specifically on labeling it 'GA' if you know most real users will struggle without a UI, since that mislabels the product's actual readiness.

plain: Smartphones are engineered, often deliberately, to be hard to put down. Apps use variable reward schedules, similar to slot machines, where notifications, likes, or new content arrive unpredictably, which keeps people checking compulsively. Social media and video apps use infinite scroll and autoplay to remove natural stopping points that used to exist with, say, a newspaper or a TV show ending. Beyond design, phones also serve real needs: they're how people stay connected to friends and family, get news, manage work, and fill small pockets of downtime like waiting in line. There's also a psychological pull toward novelty and social comparison, since seeing what others are doing triggers curiosity and sometimes anxiety about missing out. Combined, these factors create habits that feel automatic rather than deliberate, which is why many people report using their phones more than they consciously intend to.
